q: In the root Cargo.toml, `[workspace.lints.clippy]` with `string_slice = "warn"` means:
options: Slicing a String by byte range triggers a workspace-wide warning because boundary errors panic or corrupt text
All string slicing is forbidden and rejected at compile time by rustc itself
The lint only applies to test code
Slicing is fine as long as the project compiles in release mode
explanation: clippy lints surface as warnings; rustc does not hard-reject slicing.
Workspace lints apply to the whole workspace, tests included.
Release-mode compilation has no influence on this lint.

options: Runs clippy over lib, bins, tests AND examples, treating every warning as a hard error
Runs clippy only on the default (lib) target and deletes warnings
Formats code and then lints it
Runs rustc's built-in deny lints but not clippy's
explanation: --all-targets widens coverage to tests/examples/benches; nothing is deleted.
fmt is a separate command (cf. check-everything running both).
`-D warnings` applies to clippy output; rustc built-ins are not the subject here.

q: Why would a review reject a PR full of `#[allow(clippy::...)]` attributes?
options: Allows hide problems instead of fixing them, and churn diff noise without improving code
Attributes are slower to compile than fixes
GitHub blocks files with more than two allow attributes
clippy strips all attributes when CI runs it
explanation: Compile-time cost of attributes is negligible.
No such GitHub rule exists.
clippy respects attributes — that's precisely why blanket allows are dangerous.

q: Complete this: `let initials = full_name.get(0..2).unwrap_or("??");` — compared to `&full_name[0..2]`, the get() form:
options: Returns None at slices landing mid-character instead of panicking, and the default is an explicit reviewer-visible decision
Always returns two complete characters regardless of the input byte length
Is identical but slower at compile time
Only compiles under the 2021 edition
explanation: get(0..2) still counts BYTES; multibyte text can still yield None — that's precisely what the default handles.
Compile-time behavior is unrelated; the difference is the Option return type.
get/slicing on ranges is edition-independent.

options: The team deliberately chose not to chase this stylistic lint — lint policy is a decision, not a default
The lint is disabled because it is unsound and crashes the compiler
Format arguments are never inlined in goose because of a runtime bug
The workspace has no format! macro calls anywhere
explanation: It's a style lint; 'allow' is a policy choice, not a soundness workaround.
Inlining relates to style, not runtime behavior of format!.
'Allow' does not mean 'absent' — the lint simply accepts the code as-is.

q: You found a clippy warning in goose core code. Which fix path would a goose maintainer most likely prefer?
options: A focused hand-fix at the source in a single-purpose PR, with clippy green at -D warnings
cargo clippy --fix across the entire workspace in one sweep, then commit
Adding #[allow] to every warning site to silence the pipeline
Fixing warnings only if the same line also needs a feature change
explanation: --fix sweeps produce huge unreviewable diffs where semantics-adjacent rewrites hide bugs (get() defaults!).
Allows hide problems; reviewers reject unexplained silence.
Cleanups are valid standalone PRs — coupling them to features violates single-purpose discipline.

q: Fix this compile error: `error: the non-ASCII text 'José Mouse' was sliced at a non-character boundary [:4]` — emphasis: the program panicked at runtime, not compile time. The intended fix is:
options: Switch the byte slice to .get() with an explicit fallback, deciding what truncated or missing initials mean downstream
Cast full_name to bytes and slice the resulting array
Set $env:RUST_LOG=error so the panic is swallowed
Constrain all names in the codebase to ASCII at input time
explanation: Slicing bytes still loses characters the same way — the boundary problem persists.
RUST_LOG controls logs, not panics.
Forcing ASCII ignores real users; the text domain stays Unicode.
